scope: Three current basic Create panels and their three real-source transfer panels against the actual user-criticized published 0.4.3 candidates; first formal visual review in this refinement loop.
independence: Opened actual images and adopted specs/captions. Did not read implementation scripts or other agents' visual reports. Preferences were sent to parent before supplied numeric/export evidence was read. A visual_review field embedded in the numeric heatmap evidence was ignored.

paper_references.comparison_scope: Observable layer separation, crisp outlines, alignment and compactness only; different data and panel sizes are not a performance comparison.
Observable neutral density outlines and colored summary hierarchy only; no demand to reproduce different scientific layers.

visible_reasons: Separate right-hand observation lanes uncover the median, IQR boundaries, whisker stems and caps obscured in the published candidate.
Tighter category spacing and brighter small marks preserve the three-cohort reading task without making each point compete with the summary.
preferences.transfer_assessment: Four cohorts remain distinguishable; corresponding box and lane share color and closest spatial pairing.
preferences.remaining_literature_gap: The sparse three-cohort task still looks like a straightforward distribution example; this is not evidence of universal journal-level polish.

visible_reasons: Thin neutral outlines are subordinate to colored IQR outlines and dark medians.
Narrower density silhouettes plus separate point lanes remove the old strong colored envelope/summary/raw-point collision.
preferences.transfer_assessment: Four-cohort transfer keeps all three layer roles visibly separate; points are not on the median or IQR edges.
preferences.remaining_literature_gap: The density ends are visibly flat because the documented KDE is trimmed to observed extrema, and the raw-point lane gives an extra reading column absent from the reference. These are real differences from PROGENy, not grounds to change the density or drop observations.

visible_reasons: The compact 16-by-3 matrix eliminates excessively wide bands and makes each row a short across-depot comparison.
SC/OM/PV are separated and the 48 readable cell values supply precise lookup that the pale sequential hues cannot provide alone.
Bright single-hue map, fixed linear scale and fine cell seams keep the numerical layer organized rather than creating unrelated color categories.
preferences.transfer_assessment: Four-digit integer counts fit without collision; 0–2700 color scale and count label distinguish this transfer from percentages.
preferences.remaining_literature_gap: This remains a deliberate annotated table-like heatmap for exact small-matrix comparisons, rather than the dense large-matrix pattern reading of scWAT. Low-value cells are not discriminable by hue alone; numeric labels make that limitation explicit and usable.
preferences.round_2_assessment: Candidate still preferred to actual published old baseline; stronger pale-cell seams preserve value-first hierarchy. No new visual conflict observed.

findings.location: cohort-box and cohort-violin; candidate and four-cohort transfer observation lanes
findings.evidence: At 96 dpi the nominal 2 pt marks remain individually visible, including separated outliers, but dense portions of Kerr and Arner, E are visually fine. Their matching color and immediate proximity associate them with the neighboring summary; caption explicitly defines the categorical offset.
findings.requirement: All observations remain usable while summaries stay visible; point lanes must not imply extra categories.
findings.action: Keep the present point size as a lower bound for these examples and preserve the explicit lane explanation. Do not shrink points to make future crowded data fit; reconsider the layout instead. For grayscale use, reassess the paired-lane association.

findings.location: cohort-violin; neutral KDE outline and observed-range ends
findings.evidence: The gray outline is visible in PNG and 96 dpi PDF while the colored IQR and black median read first. The extrema have flat closures, most evident in the Krieg silhouette, unlike several pointed PROGENy shapes.
findings.requirement: Density must remain faithful to the adopted Scott KDE and observed-range trimming; aesthetic adaptation cannot fabricate density tails.
findings.action: Retain these truthful endpoints and state the rendering limitation in design guidance. A future request for smoother tails requires an explicit, scientifically appropriate KDE/support decision, not cosmetic path editing.

findings.evidence: All three aliases are clearly separated and are defined in the caption. Percentage labels include 0.058 and 0.04 without crowding; transfer four-digit counts remain inside their cells. The numbers make the image more table-like than a pattern-only heatmap.
findings.requirement: Short display labels must preserve source identity, and value annotations must serve an explicit reading task.
findings.action: Keep aliases and labels for this small exact-lookup example. Do not generalize 48 annotated cells as a default for large heatmaps; require sufficient physical cell size and an exact-value reading need.

findings.location: All examples; claim scope and literature learning
findings.evidence: The new renderings visibly apply hierarchy and proportions beyond a palette swap. The source papers have different scientific mappings, category counts, uncertainty layers and physical layouts. A few improved examples cannot measure an agent-level causal benefit.
findings.requirement: An improvement claim must remain tied to actual compared images and must not assert CNS acceptance or model generalization.
findings.action: Describe these as improved basic single-panel examples with explicit layer decisions. Keep paper mechanisms and their applicability limits in Create guidance; do not advertise verified universal CNS quality.

verdict: Current candidate preferred in all three actual published-baseline comparisons. Round 2 resolves the sole minor seam issue with actual image inspection. resolved_findings.location: depot-heatmap; pale neighboring cells in candidate and count transfer
resolved_findings.evidence: Fine blue-gray seams are visible at full-resolution PNG, but become faint between near-white low-valued cells in the 96 dpi PDF preview. Cell-center numbers and row labels still permit correct tracking; no text overlaps or lost rows were observed.
resolved_findings.requirement: Clear row/cell boundaries should support crisp, organized reading without dominating the values.
resolved_findings.action: For a further proof, consider slightly increasing seam color contrast at the same 0.35 pt width, then inspect the pale-cell rows at nominal size. Do not introduce a heavy dark grid or reduce the font.
resolved_findings.resolution: Cell border color strengthened from #D4E2EA to #B7CAD7 at unchanged 0.35 pt width. Actually opened both final heatmap PNGs and both 96 dpi PDF previews: pale-cell seams are more visible without overpowering the numbers or adding heavy grid texture.
